newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah continues to slide, tone bearish.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah continues to slide, tone bearish.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah continued to slide against the dollar in late morning trade on Thursday on political jitters, dealers said.

They said worries that the upcoming campaign for the general elections could lead to unrest triggered early dollar buying, which spurred the U.S. currency through the resistance level of 2,430 at 0430 GMT. Spot rupiah was last at 2,435.0, down from the 2,420.5/21.5 open.
"It's more politics now. There is no rumour or things like that in the market. It's purely based on concern over possible unrest or riots during the campaign," one dealer said.
The campaign for the May 29 election starts on Sunday.

The local bank dealer said stop-loss buying was triggered after the dollar broke through the resistance level of 2,430 decisively. "Many operators are forced to cut losses. Stop-loss buying emerged in the late morning," he said.
Dealers said the tone was biddish for the dollar, which was expected to continue in the short-term.

The dealer said swap rates were edging up as offshore operators hedged their positions. One-month swaps were at 12.50/13.25, two at 25.5/26.0, three at 36.0/37.0 and six at 72.75/73.75 points. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
